01_member_entry.note: The encoding is domain ‖ version ‖ 0x01 ‖ LEN(pub) ‖ LEN(jid) ‖ u8(role) ‖ u64be(joined_epoch). Every entry is the same length because both variable fields are length-prefixed, not because either is fixed.

cases.note: same JID as bob, different key: a different member (§3)

02_member_set.note: Sorted by the 57-byte identity key as unsigned bytes. The JID order is given only to show it differs: an implementation that sorts by JID produces a different hash and every signature over it fails.

03_genesis.note: group_id binds the founder's identity key, so two groups collide only if that key does. previous_state_hash at epoch 0 is 64 zero bytes.

04_join.note: transition_data is the joining member_entry. The receiver applies it to the parent set and recomputes the hash (condition 7); the commit does not get to assert it.

05_leave.note: LEAVE is self-signed and needs no evidence under any policy. transition_data is the leaving identity_pub, not a member_entry.

06_membership_replacement.note: A REVOKE followed by a JOIN of a different device holding the same JID. The two member sets differ, so the two state hashes differ: an implementation that deduplicates by JID produces the wrong hash for the second one.

07_state_chain.note: Each epoch's previous_state_hash is the parent's state_hash. A chain cannot be verified from a state alone: it is the linkage that is checked.

08_concurrent_commits.note: DIFFERENT signers off the same parent. Benign. Resolved by the numerically lower commit_id, comparing 64 bytes unsigned big-endian -- never by arrival order or timestamp. Applying this rule to §8.2 is the mistake the spec exists to prevent.

09_equivocation.note: The SAME signer, two valid commits, one parent. This is an attack, not concurrency. An implementation MUST branch on who signed BEFORE it compares any commit_id.
09_equivocation.why_lowest_is_recorded: So a test can assert the implementation did NOT pick it. A conforming implementation reaches no winner here at all.

10_commit_id_determinism.note: Ed448 signing is deterministic, so the same commit body signed by the same key twice yields byte-identical signatures and one commit_id. A vector set could not exist otherwise. This is a property of Ed448, NOT a security requirement of the protocol: an implementation using a randomised signature scheme would still be sound, and would fail this vector.

11_ed448_signatures.note: Produced by ed448_rfc8032.py, which reproduces the RFC 8032 §7.4 vectors exactly. These are raw Ed448 over the given message with an empty context -- no group domain separator is applied here; that belongs to the structures being signed.

12_invalid_signatures.note: Every case here is a well-formed commit body.

cases.name: signature bit flipped
cases.reason: signature does not verify under signer_identity_pub

cases.name: signed by a key other than signer_identity_pub
cases.reason: the body names alice as signer; the signature verifies only under mallory's key

13_wrong_parent.note: Each of these is correctly signed. They must be rejected on the state check, before or regardless of the signature -- and rejected, not queued as 'the future'.

cases.name: applies to an older parent
cases.reason: previous_state_hash is not the receiver's head (condition 2)

cases.name: parent hash never existed
cases.reason: unlinkable parent: a fork (§8.3), surfaced not resolved

14_unauthorised_signers.note: Condition 4 is what makes revocation cryptographic rather than advisory: the revoked key is absent from every subsequent parent member set, so its commits fail forever without any revocation list being consulted.

cases.name: signed by a revoked device
cases.reason: signer is not in the parent member set (condition 4)

cases.name: signed by a device that was never a member
cases.reason: condition 4; note it is also a self-JOIN, which no policy authorises

cases.name: JOIN signed by a non-admin under ADMIN_ONLY
cases.reason: policy 0x01 requires role = ADMIN for JOIN (condition 6)

15_malformed_encodings.note: §2's re-encoding rule: reject a structure whose re-encoding does not reproduce the bytes received. It MUST be enforced on receipt, not on send -- a sender that happens to be canonical proves nothing about a peer.

cases.name: eight-byte length prefixes
cases.reason: LEN is four bytes big-endian (§1). An eight-byte prefix in a Rust draft made every frame fail its tag with no diagnostic.

cases.name: member entry carrying the member-set context tag
trailing byte after a complete member entry
cases.reason: re-encoding does not reproduce the input (§2)

cases.name: group_id of 31 bytes
cases.reason: group_id is 32 bytes (§1.1); the length prefix parses, the value is still wrong

cases.name: member set in descending key order
cases.reason: members are sorted ascending by identity key (§2)

cases.name: count field larger than the entries present
cases.reason: truncated input; must not be read past the end

16_complete_verification.note: One fixture carrying everything the eight conditions need. A verifier given the parent state and this commit must accept; each mutation listed must be rejected for the stated condition.

conditions.4: signer is in the parent member set and not revoked
conditions.6: ADMIN_ONLY: signer is ADMIN in the parent; evidence empty
conditions.7: applying transition_data to the parent set reproduces new_member_set_hash
conditions.8: the commit re-encodes to the bytes received

17_threshold_votes.note: The tally is evidence, not a claim: the committer includes the votes it counted and every other member re-tallies them. The revocation target's own vote MUST NOT count, and a vote binds the hash of the proposal, not only its id.

18_message_envelope.note: The envelope is NOT signed, deliberately: the two-party channel already authenticates the sender deniably, and a signature would replace a deniable property with a non-deniable one. There is no signature field to omit -- an implementation that adds one is not implementing this specification.
